description: Source and provenance ledger for the rich-v1 editorial revision. All claims remain anchored to sources verified for the frozen pilot release on 2026-08-08. reverified_on is set only where the revising editor re-read the source while preparing rich-v1. No source claims were changed without that check.

source_files_revised.note: Input is read-only. rich-v1 does not modify the frozen pilot queue or its approved release.

sources.label: NASA Science — Venus: Facts
sources.supports: Rotation period about 243 Earth days, orbital period about 225 days, retrograde rotation.
sources.media_policy: NASA still imagery is normally public domain with a requested credit line; confirm per-image credit on the NASA page before download. Never mirror assets into the repository.

sources.label: NASA Science — Venus solar day
sources.supports: Explicit distinction between the ~117-Earth-day solar day and the ~243-Earth-day sidereal day on Venus.
sources.media_policy: Text reference only.

sources.label: Pharmacology Biochemistry and Behavior, 1976
sources.supports: Goldfish trained over two consecutive days showed savings in relearning on day 2, used as a measure of long-term memory strength.
sources.media_policy: Journal record; figures not licensed for reuse. No imagery taken from the paper.

sources.label: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior, 1979
sources.supports: Goldfish acquired matching/oddity tasks over prolonged training, reaching performance substantially above chance.
sources.media_policy: Journal record; figures not licensed for reuse.

sources.label: Soft Matter, 2021 (Royal Society of Chemistry)
sources.supports: Cubes form within roughly the last 17% of the intestine; corner formation linked to regions of differing thickness/stiffness and uneven contractions.
sources.media_policy: RSC figures are copyrighted; do not reuse. An original editorial diagram may restate the published model, since facts are not copyrightable.

sources.label: NASA — Lunar Laser Ranging
sources.supports: Earth and Moon drift apart about 1.5 inches / 3.8 cm per year, measured with lunar retroreflectors left by Apollo crews.
sources.media_policy: NASA imagery public domain with requested credit; confirm per-image credit.

sources.label: Smithsonian Ocean — Cephalopods
sources.supports: Three-heart circulatory system (two branchial, one systemic) and copper-based hemocyanin giving blue blood.
sources.media_policy: Smithsonian web imagery mixes rights holders; use only items explicitly marked Smithsonian Open Access / CC0, otherwise NOAA or public-domain alternatives with checked credit.

sources.label: Smithsonian Ocean — How Cephalopods Change Color
sources.supports: Chromatophores in the skin and rapid, neurally controlled colour change in cephalopods.
sources.media_policy: Same Smithsonian policy as above.

sources.label: NASA Science — Total solar eclipse on August 12, 2026
sources.supports: Totality path across northern Russia, Greenland, Iceland, Spain and a small corner of Portugal; partial eclipse across much of Europe.
sources.media_policy: NASA eclipse path maps are public domain with requested NASA credit; use the official map, not a third-party redraw with unclear rights.

sources.label: NASA Science — NASA science soars during August total solar eclipse
sources.supports: NASA-funded teams will observe from a high-altitude aircraft and scientific balloons to study the corona and atmospheric effects of the eclipse.
sources.media_policy: NASA imagery public domain with requested credit.

sources.label: NOAA — What Causes Lightning and Thunder?
sources.supports: Lightning heats the air in its channel to as hot as 54,000 °F / 30,000 °C — about five times hotter than the surface of the Sun; explosive expansion of heated air creates the shockwave heard as thunder.
sources.media_policy: US federal (NOAA) imagery is public domain; page already credits illustrators by name — preserve credit.

sources.label: Animal Behaviour, 2010 — wild American crows learn and remember a threatening human face
sources.supports: Field experiment: crows captured once by a person in a distinctive mask scolded that mask for at least 2.7 years despite differences in wearer height, age, sex and gait; wording limited to the tested threatening-face paradigm.
sources.media_policy: Elsevier figures are copyrighted; do not reuse. Original editorial diagram is acceptable.

sources.label: UC Davis / Science, 2016 — Sunflowers move by the clock
sources.supports: Growing sunflowers use their circadian clock to track the Sun east-to-west and return east at night; mature flowers settle facing east; east-facing flowers warm faster in the morning and attracted about five times more pollinators; quotes by Stacey Harmer verified verbatim on the page.
sources.media_policy: UC Davis newsroom photo is credited (Chris Nicolini, UC Davis) — rights reserved; prefer original or CC0/Pixabay-grade imagery with checked licence, or an editorial diagram of the daily path.

sources.label: Smithsonian Ocean — Sharks
sources.supports: First sharks evolved more than 400 million years ago; oldest confirmed shark scales about 420 million years old.
sources.media_policy: Mixed rights on Smithsonian pages; prefer NOAA Ocean Service PD imagery or own timeline diagram.

sources.label: ESA — Tiny animals survive exposure to space
sources.supports: About 3000 tardigrades exposed during the Foton-M3/TARDIS experiment for 12 days; some survived vacuum and cosmic radiation.
sources.media_policy: ESA multimedia is generally CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO—check the stated licence beside each asset; attribution required; never rehost licence-ambiguous files.

sources.label: ESA HREDA — TARDIS dataset
sources.supports: Dataset page published 22 May 2026 and updated 9 July 2026; links the TARDIS experiment and the 2008 Current Biology publication.
sources.media_policy: Data page; no imagery needed from it.

sources.label: Purdue Materials Engineering — Eiffel Tower thermal expansion
sources.supports: The iron structure expands and contracts by about 15 cm between the hottest and the coldest day.
sources.media_policy: Educational page; no imagery reused from it.

sources.label: Official Eiffel Tower site — Why does the Eiffel Tower change size?
sources.supports: Asymmetric solar heating makes the top drift away from the Sun and trace a curve of roughly 15 cm in diameter over a clear day.
sources.media_policy: Site imagery rights reserved; rely on openly licensed or original imagery instead.

sources.label: Kew Gardens — Cavendish banana
sources.supports: Banana fruits are botanically classified as berries; the berry criterion is a fruit developing from a single flower with a single ovary.
sources.media_policy: Kew imagery generally rights reserved; prefer editorial photographs/diagrams.

sources.label: Proceedings of the Royal Society B, 2013 — Decades-long social memory in bottlenose dolphins
sources.supports: Playback study with former tank mates: stronger response to familiar signature whistles, including after separations of more than 20 years; author Jason N. Bruck, University of Chicago, describes it as the first study to show social recognition lasting at least 20 years in a non-human species.
sources.media_policy: Open-access text (© 2013 The Author(s), Published by the Royal Society); figures not reused. Photography from NOAA or checked open-licence sources only.
